nodes.summary: For every sequence $c : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the crease interleaving by $c$, from start index $1$, of the approximant $A_2 = (1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1)$ of Cloitre's sequence is $(1, 1, c_1, 2, c_2, 1, 1, c_3, 1, 1, c_4)$: each of the four letters $(1, 1)$, $(2)$, $(1, 1)$, $(1, 1)$ of $A_2$ is followed by its crease $c_1$, $c_2$, $c_3$, $c_4$ in turn.
nodes.title: Crease interleaving of the Cloitre approximant $A_2$

nodes.summary: Given a sequence $c : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a start index $j$, the crease interleaving of a finite word $w$ of natural numbers reads $w$ from left to right as letters $(2)$ and $(1, 1)$ and inserts $c_j, c_{j+1}, c_{j+2}, \dots$ after the successive letters. Precisely, the empty word gives the empty word; a word $2, w'$ gives $2, c_j$ followed by the interleaving of $w'$ from index $j + 1$; a word…
nodes.title: Interleaving creases into a Cloitre word

nodes.summary: Let $a_0$ be an integer, let $t$ be even and let $a_1, \dots, a_t$ be integers with $a_i \ge 1$ for every $i$, and let $q$ be the denominator in lowest terms of the value $[a_0; a_1, \dots, a_t]$ of the finite continued fraction. Then for every integer $x \ge 1$, $[a_0; a_1, \dots, a_t] + 1/(x q^2) = [a_0; a_1, \dots, a_t, x, -a_t, \dots, -a_1]$.
nodes.title: Folding lemma for finite continued fractions

nodes.summary: For every integer $a$ and all integers $l_1, \dots, l_n$ with $n \ge 0$, $[a; l_1, \dots, l_n] = a + [l_1; l_2, \dots, l_n]^{-1}$, where the empty continued fraction (the case $n = 0$) has value $0$ and $0^{-1}$ is taken to be $0$ whenever $[l_1; l_2, \dots, l_n] = 0$.
nodes.title: Recursion for finite continued fractions

nodes.summary: Let $x \ge 0$ be an integer, let $t \ge 2$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_t$ be integers with $a_i \ge 1$ for every $i$. Then for every finite list of integers $b_1, \dots, b_m$ ($m \ge 0$), the finite continued fractions satisfy $[b_1, \dots, b_m, x, -a_t, -a_{t-1}, \dots, -a_1] = [b_1, \dots, b_m, x - 1, 1, a_t - 1, a_{t-1}, \dots, a_1]$.
nodes.title: Normalizing a negated block

nodes.summary: The finite continued fraction $[1; 2, 2]$ has value $7/5$.
nodes.title: The continued fraction $(1; 2, 2)$

nodes.summary: For every integer $a$, the finite continued fraction $[a]$ has value $a$.
nodes.title: Continued fraction of length one

nodes.summary: For all integers $a$ and $b$ and all finite lists of integers $u_1, \dots, u_m$ and $v_1, \dots, v_n$ ($m, n \ge 0$), the finite continued fractions satisfy $[u_1, \dots, u_m, a, 0, b, v_1, \dots, v_n] = [u_1, \dots, u_m, a + b, v_1, \dots, v_n]$.
nodes.title: A zero partial quotient merges its neighbours

nodes.summary: For a finite list $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_t$ of integers (possibly zero or negative), the value $[a_0; a_1, \dots, a_t]$ is the rational number $a_0 + 1/(a_1 + 1/(\cdots + 1/a_t))$, computed from the right: the empty list has value $0$, and the list $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_t$ has value $a_0 + v^{-1}$, where $v$ is the value of the list $a_1, \dots, a_t$. In particular $[a] = a + 0^{-1} = a$; here and at any vanishing…
nodes.title: Value of a finite continued fraction

nodes.summary: Let $x_k = 6$ for every $k$, and let $A_0 = (1, 1)$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k\,(x_{k+1} - 1)\,A_k^r$, where the mirror image $A^r$ of a word $A$ is obtained by reversing $A$ and then replacing a leading $2$ by $1, 1$, or two leading letters $1, 1$ by $2$, leaving any other word unchanged. Then $A_2 = (1, 1, 5, 2, 5, 1, 1, 5, 1, 1)$.
nodes.title: The paperfolding continued-fraction word $A_2$ for constant $x_k = 6$

nodes.summary: For every sequence $x$ of natural numbers, the continued-fraction word $A_1$ defined by $x$ is $(1, 1, \max(x_1 - 1, 0), 2)$.
nodes.title: The second paperfolding continued-fraction word

nodes.summary: For a sequence $x = (x_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of natural numbers, the finite words $A_k$ of natural numbers are defined by $A_0 = (1, 1)$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k \, (x_{k+1} - 1) \, A_k^r$: the concatenation of $A_k$, the single letter $\max(x_{k+1} - 1, 0)$ and the mirror image $A_k^r$ of $A_k$. Let $A_k$ be the continued-fraction words defined by $x$, so that $A_0 = (1, 1)$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k \, (x_{k+1} - 1) \, A_k^r$, where the mirror image $A^r$ of a word $A$ is…

nodes.title: Second term of the paperfolding sums

nodes.summary: For every sequence $x$ of natural numbers and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the paperfolding sum terms defined by $x$ satisfy $s_{k+1} = s_k^2 / x_k$, where the quotient is read as $0$ when $x_k = 0$.

nodes.summary: For a sequence $x = (x_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of natural numbers, the real numbers $s_k$ are defined by $s_0 = 1$ and $s_{k+1} = s_k^2 / x_k$, where the quotient is read as $0$ when $x_k = 0$. They are the terms of the sums $S = \sum_k s_k$.
nodes.title: Terms of the paperfolding sums

nodes.summary: Let $A_k$ be the $k$-th approximant of Cloitre's sequence. As $k \to \infty$, the proportion of entries of $A_k$ equal to $1$ tends to $2/3$, and the proportion of entries equal to $2$ tends to $1/3$.

Combinatorics

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
